Dear Kalinga,

Greetings and good day! I pray that you and your team are in good health and in good spirits. I would like to thank you for being part of my journey as a scholar. Before I begin, I would like to thank you for your generosity and patience. Let me tell you about how my month went.

For this month, we finished our midterm examinations. I am currently in my third year taking Bachelor of Elementary Education. I received 2.25 in Child Development and 2.25 in Mathematics for Teachers. I passed all of my subjects. We also started working on our research paper, and the deadline for the first part is next month. I have not yet received my grade in Assessment of Learning because the results have not been released.

I keep a notebook for important dates and deadlines so that I will not forget them. I would like to study more often, but I am still adjusting my routine.

My father is a fisherman in Bulacan, and my mother is the owner of a small sari-sari store. My younger brother is in Grade 2 and does well in school. The situation of our family is the same as in the previous month.

This month, the water supply in our area was interrupted for a day, and we had to fetch water from a neighbor's deep well. It took some time every morning, but we were able to finish our household tasks before class.

I would like to thank you again for everything that you do for us. I will not forget your kindness, and I will use this opportunity well. It is a big blessing to be part of your scholarship program. May the Lord bless you abundantly for your generosity.

Your scholar,
Trisha L. Domingo

Dear Kalinga,

Good day, Kalinga! I hope that this letter reaches you while you are in good health. Before I begin, I would like to thank you for your generosity and patience. I would like to give you an update about my studies and my family.

For this month, I am happy to share that I did well in our midterm examinations. I am currently in my first year taking Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Management, and I received 1.5 in Culinary Arts and 1.5 in Hospitality Marketing. I am proud of these results because I worked hard for them. Our group received a high mark for the project that we submitted on October 4, and our teacher praised our work. I have not yet received my grade in Tourism Management because the results have not been released.

To continue improving myself, I ask my teachers questions after class and join a study group with my classmates. I volunteered to tutor two Grade 3 pupils in our barangay every Saturday, which taught me to be more patient.

My father is a construction worker in Pampanga, and my mother is a laundrywoman. We are thankful that we are all healthy and that we still eat dinner together almost every night.

This month, our house experienced a brownout for two days because of repairs by the electric company, so it was difficult to study at night. My aunt lent us a rechargeable lamp, and I was able to finish my assignments.

Thank you for the help that you give to me and to my family. I will not forget your kindness, and I will use this opportunity well. Your scholarship has helped me not only in school but also in my daily needs. Please take care, and may God continue to bless you.

Your scholar,
Erika C. Zamora

Good day, Kalinga! I hope this letter finds you in good health. Thank you for never getting tired of supporting students like me. Before I begin, I would like to thank you for your generosity and patience. I hope you will not mind if I share the important things that happened to me this month.

I want to improve my grades, but I still need to learn how to manage my time. I sometimes study during recess and lunch break, though I find it hard to remember what I read.

My father is a factory worker in Davao, and my mother is a house helper. My two younger siblings are both in elementary school, and I help them whenever I have free time. We are all safe, but my parents are worried about our daily needs.

My youngest sibling was confined in the hospital for a week because of a fever, and my parents had to spend a great deal of money for the medicines. I was the one who watched over our house in the evenings, so I was unable to study properly. I felt anxious about my family and about my own studies. My sibling is now at home and recovering, and I am trying to catch up with the lessons that I missed.

Thank you for the help that you give to me and to my family. It is a big blessing to be part of your scholarship program. I hope that you will continue to help students like me. Please take care, and may God continue to bless you.

Your scholar,
Christian N. Tolentino
